onePrimaryObject.name: Sponge
onePrimaryObject.scope: One primary object; ordinary supporting objects may be present.

everydayGoal.source: Clear a puddle from the floor so the door can open.

audits.openingAudit: A transparent cube beside a squeezed sponge does not establish, in one still, that this is liquid water just extracted from that sponge. The door obstruction is described, but its functional cause remains unresolved.

oneImmutableRule.declared: Whenever Mimi squeezes the wet sponge, its absorbed water drops out as one rigid transparent cube of the same volume.

stableTrigger.declared: Mimi compresses the visibly swollen sponge between her palms.

perBeat.exactRule: Whenever Mimi squeezes the wet sponge, its absorbed water drops out as one rigid transparent cube of the same volume.

source.strategy: Mimi pushes the door with her shoulder while finishing the squeeze.
source.visibleConsequence: The door stops against the water cube, leaving only a narrow gap.
source.newInformation: The extracted water is solid enough to block the door.

perBeat.sourceComparison: Finishing the squeeze and blocking the door fits a solid water output; volume is not quantitatively established.

perBeat.exactRule: Whenever Mimi squeezes the wet sponge, its absorbed water drops out as one rigid transparent cube of the same volume.

source.strategy: She slides the cube away from the door and uses the sponge to absorb the remaining broad puddle.
source.visibleConsequence: The door's opening arc becomes dry, but the sponge bulges between her hands.
source.newInformation: The liquid can be cleared, provided she finds somewhere else to squeeze.

perBeat.sourceComparison: Absorption and manually sliding an existing cube do not add a new impossible behavior. The accepted audit nevertheless leaves this beat ambiguous.

perBeat.exactRule: Whenever Mimi squeezes the wet sponge, its absorbed water drops out as one rigid transparent cube of the same volume.

source.strategy: Mimi reaches through the narrow door gap and squeezes the sponge on the other side.
source.visibleConsequence: A larger water cube drops outside the room, directly behind the door.
source.newInformation: Moving the squeeze outside has placed the new block on the opposite side of the same door.

perBeat.sourceComparison: Squeezing outside creates a cube outside; the larger cube is compatible with more absorbed water, but volume equality is not measurable from this prose.

perBeat.exactRule: Whenever Mimi squeezes the wet sponge, its absorbed water drops out as one rigid transparent cube of the same volume.

source.strategy: She stands on the dry floor and confidently pulls the door open.
source.visibleConsequence: The door wedges between the two transparent water cubes, framing Mimi in a perfectly dry doorway too narrow to pass through.
source.newInformation: She has removed the entire puddle but converted it into a solid doorstop on both sides.

perBeat.sourceComparison: A solid cube can obstruct a door without a new rule. Spatial continuity is unclear: beat 2 moved the first cube away, and its final return to the opening arc is not described.

payoff.sourceConcern: Door/cube spatial continuity is unresolved; no new squeeze rule is stated.

onePrimaryObject.name: Broom
onePrimaryObject.scope: One primary object; ordinary supporting objects may be present.

everydayGoal.source: Sweep a small heap of dirt into a dustpan.

audits.openingAudit: The continuous floor visibly folds and obstructs the dirt route. Bristles against the foot of a fold do not establish from a still that forward broom travel creates it, or that stroke length determines height.

oneImmutableRule.declared: Whenever Kiko pushes the broom forward against the floor, the traversed strip of floor folds into a permanent upright pleat as tall as that stroke is long, carrying anything resting on that strip upward with it.

stableTrigger.declared: The broom head pressed against the floor during a forward push.

perBeat.exactRule: Whenever Kiko pushes the broom forward against the floor, the traversed strip of floor folds into a permanent upright pleat as tall as that stroke is long, carrying anything resting on that strip upward with it.

source.strategy: Kiko lifts the broom over the little fold and gives the dirt a short forward shove.
source.visibleConsequence: A second, knee-high floor pleat rises beneath the dirt, leaving the dustpan below it.
source.newInformation: Reaching over the first obstacle creates a taller obstacle under the target.

perBeat.sourceComparison: A forward shove produces a floor pleat beneath the dirt. Short is relative, so a knee-high result is not an exact length contradiction; floor contact is implied rather than fully staged.

perBeat.exactRule: Whenever Kiko pushes the broom forward against the floor, the traversed strip of floor folds into a permanent upright pleat as tall as that stroke is long, carrying anything resting on that strip upward with it.

source.strategy: Kiko steps onto the first pleat and stretches the broom across the second for a longer sweep.
source.visibleConsequence: The longer swept strip becomes a waist-high pleat with the dirt balanced on top.
source.newInformation: The length of the sweep determines the height of the new obstruction.

perBeat.sourceComparison: A longer sweep produces a higher pleat and preserves existing obstacles, consistent with the same rule; exact lengths remain unspecified.

perBeat.exactRule: Whenever Kiko pushes the broom forward against the floor, the traversed strip of floor folds into a permanent upright pleat as tall as that stroke is long, carrying anything resting on that strip upward with it.

source.strategy: Kiko climbs onto the knee-high pleat and places both feet immediately behind the dirt on the waist-high strip.
source.visibleConsequence: Kiko and the dirt share a narrow elevated strip, with the dustpan clearly visible far below.
source.newInformation: Kiko has reached the dirt, but now stands on the floor that the broom will fold.

perBeat.sourceComparison: Climbing changes Kiko’s position without triggering a new fold. The accepted audit leaves this non-trigger beat ambiguous. Placement of both feet on the waist-high strip needs visual staging review.

perBeat.exactRule: Whenever Kiko pushes the broom forward against the floor, the traversed strip of floor folds into a permanent upright pleat as tall as that stroke is long, carrying anything resting on that strip upward with it.

source.strategy: Kiko reaches the broom behind both heels and makes one long forward sweep beneath the feet toward the dirt.
source.visibleConsequence: The occupied strip folds into a towering pleat, leaving Kiko and the dirt together on its narrow summit above the untouched dustpan.
source.newInformation: The broom carries the sweeper upward by exactly the same mechanism that carries the dirt.

perBeat.sourceComparison: Sweeping the occupied strip raises its occupants under the declared carry-anything rule. Summit balance and broom reach are staging uncertainties, not explicit rule mutation.

payoff.sourceConcern: Kiko being carried follows the explicit anything-on-strip clause. Reach/balance are source-staging uncertainties.

onePrimaryObject.name: Clothes iron
onePrimaryObject.scope: One primary object; ordinary supporting objects may be present.

audits.openingAudit: Smooth cloth and a buckled supporting board are simultaneously described, but the exact crease-transfer relationship and cause are not established in one still. The iron is planted rather than shown removing a matched crease.

oneImmutableRule.declared: Whenever the iron presses a crease out of the shirt, an identical crease forms in the ironing board directly beneath that crease.

stableTrigger.declared: The iron presses a raised shirt crease flat.

perBeat.exactRule: Whenever the iron presses a crease out of the shirt, an identical crease forms in the ironing board directly beneath that crease.

source.strategy: Mimi slides the iron across the shirt's wrinkled middle.
source.visibleConsequence: The shirt's middle becomes smooth while the board beneath it buckles into a broad ridge, tipping the remaining wrinkles toward Mimi.
source.newInformation: A larger shirt crease produces the same larger fold in the supporting board.

perBeat.sourceComparison: Smoothing the middle while the support ridges fits transfer beneath the crease. Exact identical crease shape is asserted, not geometrically demonstrated.

perBeat.exactRule: Whenever the iron presses a crease out of the shirt, an identical crease forms in the ironing board directly beneath that crease.

source.strategy: Mimi pulls the wrinkled hem onto the board's remaining flat end and presses it.
source.visibleConsequence: The hem flattens, but the board's end folds upward, leaving the shirt draped between two raised sections.
source.newInformation: Moving to unused support only relocates the accumulating board creases.

perBeat.sourceComparison: Moving the hem to flat support and folding that end follows the same transfer condition.

perBeat.exactRule: Whenever the iron presses a crease out of the shirt, an identical crease forms in the ironing board directly beneath that crease.

source.strategy: Mimi stretches the last wrinkled sleeve across the board's central ridge and presses along it.
source.visibleConsequence: The sleeve smooths as a new crease folds the ridge into a compact accordion, leaving almost no level working surface.
source.newInformation: The existing board folds remain while each newly removed shirt crease adds another.

perBeat.sourceComparison: Adding another crease while older folds remain fits accumulation, but an identical crease folding an existing ridge into a compact accordion needs geometry review; accepted status is ambiguous.

perBeat.exactRule: Whenever the iron presses a crease out of the shirt, an identical crease forms in the ironing board directly beneath that crease.

source.strategy: Mimi presses the final cuff crease against the accordion's small flat top, then lifts the shirt by its shoulders.
source.visibleConsequence: Mimi holds up a perfectly smooth shirt above an ironing board crumpled into a giant shirt-shaped set of wrinkles.
source.newInformation: The shirt is flat because its entire collection of creases now occupies the board.

perBeat.sourceComparison: The final cuff press and lifting the shirt use the same trigger. The entire board becoming shirt-shaped is not entailed by arbitrary repositioned crease transfers. It may describe a silhouette rather than a new mechanism; this remains ambiguous.

payoff.sourceConcern: The shirt-shaped final arrangement is not fully supported by the described spatial mapping of each transferred crease; no explicit second mechanism is introduced.
